subject: Post-call recap: traffic profile & p95 targets — ClearSight Health discovery
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@clearsighthealth.com>, Michael Chu <michael.chu@clearsighthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: traffic profile & p95 targets — ClearSight Health discovery

Hi Elena / Michael — thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Pain points you shared
- Production p95 for streaming endpoints ~1.1–1.4s under moderate load; user experience shows stalls at session peaks.
- Queueing / head-of-line delays when batches form; clients need interactivity (partial tokens streamed) rather than large delayed chunks.
- Cost is a factor — currently running multiple replicas to hit concurrency which is eating margin.

Current stack (as described)
- Model serving: Triton on AWS ECS with 4x A10g-equivalent GPUs, custom batching disabled, inference logic in a Node frontend.
- Observability: basic CloudWatch + custom traces, not capturing per-token timing.
- Traffic: mostly chat-like sessions, median 90–140 tokens per response, peak concurrent sessions ~250.

Success criteria you described
- p95 streaming latency <= 350ms for interactive responses at target concurrency (we heard ~200–300 concurrent sessions).
- Smooth token streaming every ~150–250ms (no 1s+ gaps).
- Unit cost reduction goal: 20–30% while meeting latency targets.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
1) You to share: representative traffic capture (sample traces, client logs) and a short cost snapshot (monthly inference spend).
2) Redwood to run a quick baseline: ingest trace and return a focused report with probable bottlenecks (batching, kernel choice, KV caching). Target: 3 business days after we get traces.
3) Technical deep-dive: 60–90m session with infra + ML engineer to validate assumptions and pick an approach (optimizations vs. different serving topology).
4) Pilot proposal: 2–3 week trial with a small reserved pool and telemetry — we'll propose measurable acceptance criteria (p95, token cadence, cost).

Questions for you now
- Can you confirm peak sustained RPS during your busiest 10-minute windows?
- Do you require region restriction (we heard mostly US but want to confirm)?
- Any compliance constraints (SOC2 / data residency) beyond standard HIPAA-adjacent controls?

Attachments: placeholder for the traffic sample you mentioned — if convenient, drop into the Drive link below or send directly.

I'll coordinate the deep-dive once we have the traces. Marissa / Ben — looping you for pilot/contract path and internal resource allocation.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference runtime
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@clearsighthealth.com>

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: traffic profile & p95 targets — ClearSight Health discovery

Thanks, Diego — this is great and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications and I attached a small sample trace (sample-trace-20270516.jsonl) via Drive link.

Clarifications
- Peak sustained: about 180–220 concurrent sessions during business hours; spikes up to ~320 for short bursts (2–3 minutes).
- Typical session token shape: initial prompt 40–80 tokens, responses 60–160 tokens; streaming granularity desired = every 200ms if possible.
- Function calls: we use tool-calling for external data enrichment (~12% of requests), payload sizes small but end-to-end latency matters.
- Compliance: SOC2 in progress, we'd like evidence of audit logs and KMS support.

Attachments shared
- sample-trace-20270516.jsonl (contains 30 sessions, anonymized) — link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-clearsight-traffic-samples

We're interested in the on-prem/private option if that materially affects latency, but still evaluating hosted + dedicated pools first.

Happy to schedule the technical deep-dive — are you available Wed 19th morning PST?

Best,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Engineering | ClearSight Health

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: traffic profile & p95 targets — ClearSight Health discovery

Elena — thanks for the trace and the clarifications. Quick responses and action items from our side: 

What we saw (preliminary skim of trace)
- Several sessions show token bursts where client-level batching aggregates multiple small requests into 1 inference call — that amplifies tail latency.
- Token emission cadence is inconsistent in your samples (some sessions send a large chunk, then stall). This looks like client-side buffering plus server-side batching interactions.

Short-term mitigations we can propose for the deep-dive
- Disable large server-side batching for interactive endpoints and enable micro-batching (per-client continuous batching / KV-aware).
- Add a lightweight prefix K/V cache for repeated context to avoid recomputing the same embeddings/encodings.
- Kernel/quantization recommendation: run a quick micro-benchmark on your model family (we'll provide scripts) to see if int8/4 quantization preserves quality and reduces per-token time.

Proposed timeline
- Wed 19 May, 09:30 PST — technical deep-dive (60m) with your infra + ML engineer.
- By Mon 24 May — Redwood provides baseline report + recommended pilot config.

Pilot acceptance criteria (example)
- p95 streaming latency <= 350ms at 220 concurrent sessions for a 90-token median response.
- Token emission cadence: 200–250ms between first partial response and next chunk for 90% of requests.
- Cost delta: <= 25% increase vs. current spend for the pilot window, with roadmap to reduce.

Marissa / Ben — please prepare the pilot brief (resource plan + initial pricing framework) after the deep-dive. I'm happy to take point on the technical report.

Thanks,
Diego

Hi Elena — Ben here, looping in to make the deep-dive as actionable as possible. A couple quick items before Wed: 

1) Short checklist we typically ask customers to have ready for the call:
- Small reproducible trace (you've already uploaded that — great).
- Representative config snippets (serving config, batching), even if redacted.
- Sample client code showing streaming behavior (if available).

2) I attached a concise guide we often send to engineering teams: "redwood-mini-benchmark-guide.pdf" — this includes the micro-benchmark script and how to run it on one replica. If you can run it ahead of the call, we'll have immediate data to discuss.

3) Commercial/procurement pre-note: we'll scope a 2–3 week pilot agreement (trial pool) and provide a limited trial credit to offset ramp. Marissa will follow up on the pricing/contract path after the technical run.

If Wed 19th 09:30 PST still works, I'll take notes and surface the pilot deck next week.
